ko.B: 우리는 살아 계신 하나님의 성전입니다. 하나님께서 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다. "내가 그들 안에 머물러 살고 그들 가운데 다닐 것이다. 나는 그들의 하나님이 되고, 그들은 내 백성이 될 것이다."
ko.R: 우리는 살아 계신 하나님의 성전입니다. 하나님께서 직접 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다. "내가 그들 안에서 살고 그들 가운데 다니겠다. 나는 그들의 하나님이 되고, 그들은 내 백성이 될 것이다."

pt.L: Pois nós somos [o] templo [do] Deus vivo; como Deus disse: "Habitarei neles e andarei entre [eles], e serei o Deus deles, e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo."
pt.B: Afinal, nós somos o templo do Deus vivo. Como Deus disse: "Farei neles a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} morada e andarei entre eles; serei o Deus deles, e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo."
pt.R: Nós somos o templo do Deus vivo. O próprio Deus disse: "Vou morar neles e andar entre eles. Serei o Deus deles, e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo."

decisions.choice: we together are the temple of the living God
decisions.reason: "We" is plural and the temple is one: the church as a whole is the place where God lives, as in 1 Corinthians 3:16. The living God is set against lifeless idols (1 Thessalonians 1:9).

decisions.choice: Leviticus 26:11-12 with Ezekiel 37:27, from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The words join God's promise in Leviticus 26:11-12 ("I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people") with Ezekiel 37:27 ("my dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people"). Paul does not quote either word for word; Leviticus has "you" where Paul has "them". In the Hebrew of both passages the speaker is the LORD, named by the divine name.

decisions.choice: dwell in them: God living within his people
decisions.reason: Ἐνοικήσω is "live in", a stronger word than the "among" of the Old Testament passages. With ἐμπεριπατήσω ("walk about among") it describes God present with and within his people, not in a building.

decisions.choice: make my dwelling in them
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the language of a dwelling, which suits the picture of a temple (m3).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}}, {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}}, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} when God speaks in the quotations of 6:16-18; "je" without a span
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for Jesus speaking of himself: the possessive and stressed pronouns for God carry the span wherever the English "my" and "me" do, and also "et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je" in verse 17, where French needs a stressed pronoun the English lacks.

decisions.choice: "chúng ta" for "we are the temple"; "Ta" for God, "họ" for his people in the quotation (6:16-18)
decisions.reason: The whole church is God's temple, as in 1 Corinthians 3:16, so the inclusive "chúng ta". God speaks as "Ta", as in the Vietnamese Romans; "dân Ta" takes the deity_pronoun setting. "Ngự" is the word for God's dwelling, as in 1 Corinthians 3:16.

decisions.choice: God's words in the plain style ("다닐 것이다", "될 것이다") through verses 16-18
decisions.reason: As in Romans, God speaks in 해라체 in quotations of Scripture.

source.text: διὸ ἐξέλθατε ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀφορίσθητε, λέγει κύριος, καὶ ἀκαθάρτου μὴ ἅπτεσθε· κἀγὼ εἰσδέξομαι ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: Therefore come out from [the] midst of them, and be separated, says [the] Lord, and unclean not touch; and I will welcome you;

en.L: Therefore "come out from [the] midst of them and be separated," says [the] Lord, "and do not touch [anything] unclean; and I will welcome you."
en.B: So "come out from among them and keep yourselves apart," says the Lord, "and do not touch what is unclean; then I will take you in."
en.R: So the Lord says, "Come out from among them and keep yourselves separate. Do not touch anything that would make you unclean. Then I will welcome you."

fr.L: C’est pourquoi « sortez du milieu d’eux et séparez-vous », dit le Seigneur, « et ne touchez pas à [ce qui est] impur ; et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous accueillerai. »
fr.B: Ainsi, « sortez du milieu d’eux et tenez-vous à l’écart », dit le Seigneur, « et ne touchez pas à ce qui est impur ; alors je vous accueillerai. »
fr.R: Alors le Seigneur dit : « Sortez du milieu d’eux et restez séparés d’eux. Ne touchez à rien de ce qui pourrait vous rendre impurs. Alors je vous accueillerai. »

es.L: Por tanto, «{{plural_you:salgan|salid}} de en medio de ellos y {{plural_you:apártense|apartaos}}», dice [el] Señor, «y no {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} [nada] impuro; y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} recibiré».
es.B: Así que «{{plural_you:salgan|salid}} de en medio de ellos y {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} aparte», dice el Señor, «y no {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} lo que es impuro; entonces yo {{plural_you:los|os}} acogeré».
es.R: Por eso el Señor dice: «{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} de en medio de ellos y {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} separados. No {{plural_you:toquen|toquéis}} nada que {{plural_you:los|os}} haga impuros. Entonces yo {{plural_you:los|os}} recibiré».

sw.L: Kwa hiyo "tokeni katikati yao na mjitenge," asema Bwana, "wala msiguse kilicho najisi; {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawapokea."
sw.B: Kwa hiyo "ondokeni miongoni mwao na mkae mbali," asema Bwana, "wala msiguse kilicho najisi; ndipo nitawakaribisha."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Bwana anasema, "Tokeni kati yao na mkae mbali nao. Msiguse kitu chochote ambacho kingewafanya najisi. Ndipo nitawakaribisha."

vi.L: Vì vậy, "hãy ra khỏi giữa họ và hãy tách riêng ra," Chúa phán, "và đừng chạm đến [vật gì] ô uế; thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tiếp nhận các ngươi."
vi.B: Vì vậy, "hãy ra khỏi giữa họ và giữ mình tách biệt," Chúa phán, "và đừng chạm đến điều ô uế; rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tiếp nhận các ngươi."
vi.R: Vì vậy, Chúa phán: "Hãy ra khỏi giữa họ và giữ mình tách biệt. Đừng chạm đến bất cứ điều gì làm cho các ngươi bị ô uế. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tiếp đón các ngươi."

ko.L: 그러므로 주께서 말씀하신다. "너희는 그들 가운데서 나와 따로 있어라. 그리고 깨끗하지 않은 것을 만지지 마라. 그러면 내가 너희를 받아들일 것이다."
ko.B: 그러므로 주님께서 말씀하신다. "너희는 그들 가운데서 나와 따로 떨어져 있어라. 깨끗하지 않은 것을 만지지 마라. 그러면 내가 너희를 받아들이겠다."
ko.R: 그래서 주님께서 말씀하십니다. "너희는 그들 가운데서 나와 따로 떨어져 있어라. 너희를 부정하게 만드는 것은 아무것도 만지지 마라. 그러면 내가 너희를 반갑게 맞아들이겠다."

pt.L: Por isso, "saiam do meio deles e separem-se", diz [o] Senhor, "e não toquem [em nada] impuro; e eu acolherei vocês."
pt.B: Por isso, "saiam do meio deles e se mantenham separados", diz o Senhor, "e não toquem no que é impuro; então eu acolherei vocês."
pt.R: Por isso o Senhor diz: "Saiam do meio deles e fiquem separados. Não toquem em nada que torne vocês impuros. Então eu vou receber vocês."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 52:11 and Ezekiel 20:34, from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Isaiah 52:11 calls God's people to go out from Babylon and touch nothing unclean; Paul gives it in a shortened form and a different order. "I will welcome you" comes from Ezekiel 20:34 in the Greek Old Testament, where God promises to gather his people from the nations. "Says the Lord" is the prophets' formula, which in the Hebrew uses the divine name; κύριος here is the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: come out and be separate: break with idol worship and what defiles, not leave the city
alternatives: withdraw from all contact with unbelievers
decisions.reason: In context the separation is from idols (verse 16) and from "every defilement of flesh and spirit" (7:1). Unclean is the Law's word for what may not come near God, used here of what belongs to idol worship. In 1 Corinthians 5:10 Paul says believers cannot leave the world.

decisions.choice: therefore: Paul draws the conclusion from the promise of verse 16
decisions.reason: διὸ links the quotation to what comes before: because God lives among his people, they must separate from what is unclean. The quotations run on to the end of verse 18.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The Greek has κύριος, so English says "Lord", as in other New Testament quotations of the Old Testament (John 1:23); m1 notes the divine name behind it.

decisions.choice: So the Lord says, at the start
alternatives: says the Lord, in the middle
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker first so that the whole quotation can follow.

decisions.choice: najisi
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:14, "najisi" is what is ritually unclean, the sense of the quotation; "kichafu" would be merely dirty.

decisions.choice: "Chúa phán", with "Chúa", not "CHÚA"; "các ngươi" for "you" in God's words (6:17-18)
decisions.reason: As in 2:16 of the first letter: the Greek has kyrios, with the divine name behind it. God addresses his people as "các ngươi", as in the Vietnamese Romans 10:19, while Paul's own "anh chị em" stays outside the quotation.

decisions.choice: "주" (L); "주님" (B, R), with no divine_name span, here and in verse 18
decisions.reason: The prophets' words have the divine name in the Hebrew; Paul's Greek has "Lord".

decisions.choice: "주께서 말씀하신다" placed before the quotation (L, B)
alternatives: inside the quotation, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: Korean does not break a quotation for "says the Lord"; the words stand before it, as the English Readable does. The plain "말씀하신다" (L, B) keeps the voice of the prophetic formula.

decisions.choice: vocês (God speaking to his people)
decisions.reason: God addresses his people here in the plural. Portuguese has no living plural of "tu" ("vós" is not used, style guide section 4), so God says "vocês", as Jesus does to several people.

source.text: καὶ ἔσομαι ὑμῖν εἰς πατέρα, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔσεσθέ μοι εἰς υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας, λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ.

records.literal_gloss: and I will be to you for a father, and you will be to me for sons and daughters, says [the] Lord Almighty.

en.L: "And I will be a father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}," says [the] Lord Almighty.
en.B: "I will be your Father, and you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sons and daughters," declares the Lord Almighty.
en.R: "I will be your Father, and you will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sons and daughters," says the Lord, who rules over everything.

fr.L: « Et je serai pour vous un père, et vous serez pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} des fils et des filles », dit le Seigneur tout-puissant.
fr.B: « Je serai votre Père, et vous serez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} fils et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} filles », déclare le Seigneur tout-puissant.
fr.R: « Je serai votre Père, et vous serez {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} fils et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} filles », dit le Seigneur, qui règne sur tout.

es.L: «Y seré para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes serán|vosotros seréis}} para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} hijos e hijas», dice [el] Señor Todopoderoso.
es.B: «Seré {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes serán|vosotros seréis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hijos e hijas», declara el Señor Todopoderoso.
es.R: «Seré {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre, y {{plural_you:ustedes serán|vosotros seréis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hijos e hijas», dice el Señor, que gobierna sobre todas las cosas.

sw.L: "Nami nitakuwa kwenu baba, nanyi mtakuwa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} wana na binti," asema Bwana Mwenyezi.
sw.B: "Nitakuwa Baba yenu, nanyi mtakuwa wana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na binti {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}," asema Bwana Mwenyezi.
sw.R: "Nitakuwa Baba yenu, nanyi mtakuwa watoto {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, wa kiume na wa kike," asema Bwana, anayetawala vitu vyote.

vi.L: "Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ là cha của các ngươi, và các ngươi sẽ là con trai và con gái của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}," Chúa Toàn Năng phán.
vi.B: "Ta sẽ là Cha của các ngươi, và các ngươi sẽ là con trai và con gái của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}," Chúa Toàn Năng phán.
vi.R: "Ta sẽ là Cha của các ngươi, và các ngươi sẽ là con trai và con gái của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}," Chúa, là Đấng cai trị trên muôn vật, phán.

ko.L: "나는 너희에게 아버지가 되고, 너희는 나에게 아들과 딸이 될 것이다" 하고 전능하신 주께서 말씀하신다.
ko.B: "나는 너희의 아버지가 되고, 너희는 나의 아들딸이 될 것이다" 하고 전능하신 주님께서 말씀하신다.
ko.R: 모든 것을 다스리시는 주님께서 말씀하십니다. "나는 너희의 아버지가 되고, 너희는 나의 아들과 딸이 될 것이다."

pt.L: "E eu serei para vocês um pai, e vocês serão para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} filhos e filhas", diz [o] Senhor Todo-Poderoso.
pt.B: "Eu serei o Pai de vocês, e vocês serão os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} filhos e filhas", declara o Senhor Todo-Poderoso.
pt.R: "Eu serei o Pai de vocês, e vocês serão os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} filhos e filhas", diz o Senhor, que governa todas as coisas.

decisions.choice: 2 Samuel 7:14, widened to all God's people
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 7:14 God promises David about his son: "I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me." Paul makes the promise plural and adds "daughters", as God speaks of "my sons" and "my daughters" in Isaiah 43:6. What was promised to David's son is promised to all God's people.

decisions.choice: the Lord Almighty: the Lord who rules over all
decisions.reason: παντοκράτωρ means "ruler of all". The Greek Old Testament often uses it for the Hebrew title "LORD of hosts", which has the divine name; in 2 Samuel 7:8, shortly before the promise Paul quotes, God speaks as the LORD of hosts. Here κύριος is the God of Israel, as in verse 17.

decisions.choice: be a father to you; be sons and daughters to me
decisions.reason: εἰς with a noun ("be for a father") is a Hebrew way of saying "become, be as", taken over from the Greek Old Testament. "Sons and daughters" names men and women alike as God's children.

decisions.choice: the Lord Almighty (L, B); the Lord, who rules over everything (R)
alternatives: the Lord who holds all power
decisions.reason: "Almighty" is the traditional English for παντοκράτωρ; Readable explains it (m2).

decisions.choice: sons and daughters, with no reader setting
decisions.reason: The Greek names both sons and daughters, so the words are already inclusive and need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: wana na binti (L, B); watoto ... wa kiume na wa kike (R)
decisions.reason: "Wana" alone already means sons and daughters, but the Greek names both, so Swahili names both, "wana na binti" (sons and daughters), with no setting, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Bwana Mwenyezi
decisions.reason: "Mwenyezi" is the Swahili word for the Almighty, the one who rules over all (meaning decision); Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Chúa Toàn Năng" (L, B); "Chúa, là Đấng cai trị trên muôn vật" (R) for kyrios pantokrator; "con trai và con gái" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Toàn Năng" says the Lord who rules over all (m2); "Vạn Quân" (of hosts) belongs to another Hebrew title. The Greek names both sons and daughters, so no setting is needed, as the English says.

decisions.choice: "전능하신 주" (L); "전능하신 주님" (B); "모든 것을 다스리시는 주님" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the title as "ruler of all"; "전능하신" says it, and Readable explains it, as the English does. "아들과 딸" has no gender setting, since the words name both.
